title: Chapter 81 — The Economics of the Attach: Why the Ticket Is the Business
intro: The margin architecture of appliance retail and the attach arithmetic.

sections.title: Where Profit Actually Lives
sections.content:
Appliance margins are thin: 18-30 percent depending on brand and tier. A $2,000 fridge at 25 percent margin gives you $500 in gross profit. That sounds fine until you subtract payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, and delivery costs.

Now look at attach: extended warranty margin is 50-70 percent. A $200 warranty at 60 percent equals $120 gross profit. Installation margin is 40-60 percent. Accessories margin is 45-65 percent.

Without attach on that $2,000 fridge: $500 GP. With warranty, install, haul-away, and accessories: $825 GP. That is 65 percent more profit on the same customer, same floor time, same effort.

Multiply by 15 sales a month and attach rate is the difference between making a living and building wealth.

sections.title: The Attach Stack
sections.content: Present in this order: professional installation first — 'This includes a licensed technician who verifies your connections and makes sure everything is up to code.' Haul-away next — 'They will remove and recycle your old unit. You will not have to deal with it.' Extended warranty after they have committed to the product but before the write-up. Accessories last. And complementary products — 'Most customers who buy this range also need a vent hood. Want me to show you what pairs with it?'

sections.title: Attach Rate Benchmarks
sections.content:
Top performers: 35-45 percent attach rate. Store average: 18-25 percent. Below 15 percent: you are not presenting, not forgetting.

The difference between 20 percent and 40 percent attach on a $3,000 average ticket is $600 per sale in additional revenue — and attach margins are significantly higher than appliance margins.

Do not think 'I need to sell more.' Think 'I need to complete more sales.' Every uncompleted sale — no warranty, no install, no accessories — is money you left on the floor.
